thread:
SRE-Bot: INCIDENT created 1864007890 - high rate of CUDA OOMs and container restarts in serving runtime (us-west1 gpu pool). Pager triggered for oncall. severity: P1 :rotating_light:
Anna K: I’m on it. seeing bursty OOMs across ~12 pods in gpu-pool-a. autoscaler thrashing — nodes provisioning then pods CrashLoopBackOff.
Chris L: copying logs now. do we have any recent deploys to the runtime?
Maria S: no prod deploys in last 6h. I see model-variant fallback traffic spiking, many requests with long seq_len.
Platform-Eng: autoscaler metric shows sudden scale up then immediate scale down within 30-60s windows. likely low-sample noise + start-up latency causing eviction.
Anna K: first mitigation: disable horizontal autoscaling for gpu-pool-a (set min=max) to stabilize capacity. I’m running patch.
Anna K: `kubectl -n infra patch hpa gpu-pool-a-autoscaler -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":6,"maxReplicas":6}}'`
DeployBot: deploy accepted — autoscaler config updated by Anna K.
Chris L: logs from one of the failing pods: ```ERROR: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.2 GiB (GPU 0; 16.00 GiB total capacity; 11.3 GiB already allocated)
Traceback (most recent call last): ... RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory.```
Maria S: pattern: OOM spikes during initial KV cache warmup on long-context requests. KV cache is thrashing with repeated restarts.
Support Ops: any immediate customer impact observed? support queue has 6 tickets relating to timeouts in chat endpoints from enterprise customers in US-West.
Anna K: marking impact: Partial outage for hosted-generation-us-west; customers may see elevated latencies and 5xx. updating status page.
SRE-Bot: Statuspage update queued: "Degraded performance in US-West serving runtime; investigating."
Chris L: rolling a quick runtime config change: reduce max_concurrency and disable continuous-batching temporarily. That should lower memory pressure. applying via k8s configmap.
Chris L: `kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/serving-runtime MAX_CONCURRENCY=8 CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=false`
Platform-Eng: to avoid thrash we should also increase the autoscaler stabilizationWindow and add scaleDownDelay. I’ll apply: `stableWindow=300s, scaleDownDelay=600s`.
Platform-Eng: `kubectl -n infra patch hpa gpu-pool-a-autoscaler -p '{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":600}}}}'`
Maria S: temp workaround: route traffic for large-seqlen requests to cpu-backend variant (lower mem model) for customers that can tolerate latency. Setting routing policy now.
Anna K: doing canary of routing rule to 10% traffic. watch logs.
Support Ops: sending proactive note to impacted customers: "We’re aware of elevated errors in US-West; we have mitigation steps in progress and will provide updates every 15 minutes."
Chris L: after env change, pods restarted; memory usage reduced on new pods. but 4 old pods still CrashLoopBackOff due to OOM on init.
Anna K: evicting & draining crashloop pods to force restart on healthy nodes. `kubectl -n runtime delete pod serving-abc-123 --grace-period=0 --force`
Maria S: also discovered that a recent change to batcher default increased max_batch_size from 32 -> 128 in a canary config; that explains surge memory. I’m reverting that patch.
Platform-Eng: reverting canary: `kubectl -n runtime apply -f batcher-config-v1.yaml` (rollback applied).
SRE-Bot: Pager duty note: Anna K took ownership at 1864007905. Handoff pending at 1864008600 to Chris L if still active.
Anna K: current customer-facing mitigation: 1) autoscaler pinned to stable capacity 2) runtime concurrency reduced 3) large-seqlen traffic partially routed to cpu-backend 4) batcher config rolled back.
Chris L: telemetry shows 90% drop in new OOM errors after these steps. latency still elevated for some requests as caches rebuild.
Support Ops: posting update to customers: "Mitigations deployed; errors decreasing. We’ll continue to monitor and follow up." :thumbsup:
Platform-Eng: next actions: (1) tune autoscaler policies to prevent rapid scale cycles (longer stabilization, add cooldowns), (2) add prewarming for gpu nodes to reduce startup thrash, (3) add OOM early-detection to our healthchecks to avoid evict/restart loops.
Maria S: I’ll open a post-incident task for evals: detect model runs that cause high KV warmup and recommend auto-segmentation or offloading.
Chris L: preparing a short postmortem draft. will include timeline, root cause (batcher canary + autoscaler instability + long-seq KV warmup), mitigations, and action items.
Anna K: handing off to Chris L for next 2h per rotation. Chris, you have the pager.
Chris L: ack. I’m primary. Assigning follow-up issues now.
SRE-Bot: INCIDENT resolved? No — condition: degraded but stable. Will keep thread open until fully normal.
Support Ops: customers updated at 15:12 UTC.
Anna K: leaving notes in the incident board and adding affected customer list.
Chris L: plan to revert autoscaler pin once stabilization changes are live and we've observed 30m stable.
Maria S: capturing config hashes for rollback audit.
SRE-Bot: closing note scheduled in 60 minutes if no regressions. :white_check_mark:
